issues.legal_issue: The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code overrides the Electricity Act where their provisions conflict in a corporate liquidation.
Electricity dues are not government dues under the liquidation priority waterfall merely because the electricity distributor has government participation.
Electricity dues secured by a charge created under an authorized supply-code regulation and the parties’ agreement can make the electricity distributor a secured creditor.
A secured electricity distributor’s claim must be dealt with in liquidation under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code’s applicable procedures and priority rules.
